take_homes: Default to one agent. Split only for different access, dialect or stance. I would put the 'could one prompt do it?' test to any team that wants a multi-agent setup.
The failure happens at the handoffs: a number gets quietly dropped, and nothing checks the final briefing is true. I would ask for that check before any finance use.
Any agent that acts on another system needs an approval gate and a stated worst case.

monday.move: Ask the controller to try month-end variance commentary with one agent, with an approval gate before anything leaves the file. Keep it out of the multi-agent setup.
monday.stop_condition: No approval from IT for finance data, or a figure in the commentary that doesn't match the ledger.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data. I also have no cost per user per month.

misconception.why: Fully shaken it was not. The module treats agents as something you design and keep checking, with seams, rules in CLAUDE.md and risk review, and that is more than buying a licence. But nobody gave me a cost, and the shift is something I inferred myself. I still think of the tool as the main thing I would buy.

one_line: The point that you should usually use just one agent was useful, but I spent 50 minutes on it and still have no cost figure and no verified result.
